acceptedAnswer.text: Time to hire measures the calendar days between a candidate entering your recruitment process and formally accepting an employment offer. Keep the same entry definition — application date or first recruiter contact — across every comparison.

mainEntity.name: How is average time to hire calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add each completed hire’s duration, then divide by the number of completed hires. The EarlyJobs calculator uses calendar days by default: offer acceptance date minus candidate entry date.

mainEntity.name: Is time to hire the same as time to fill?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Time to fill generally starts when a vacancy is opened or approved and ends when it is filled. Time to hire starts with the candidate’s entry into the process and ends at offer acceptance.
Yes, if every record uses the same entry definition and the same date-counting method. Group by role category so warehouse, technician and office roles are not treated as interchangeable benchmarks.

mainEntity.name: Does a shorter time to hire always mean better hiring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Essential assessments, background checks and compliance steps still matter. Use the metric to spot delays and plan capacity — not to skip evaluation quality.
